@Alexander Hicks your batch request for Aristotle to prove all sorry's in ArkLib yields a counter-example: the statement of Polishchuk-Spielman (https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/ArkLib/blob/main/ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/PolishchukSpielman.lean) is not correct as written.

The model was able to prove the opposite by relying on the fact that n_x and n_y could be zero (we do not state they must be positive in the hypothesis). This makes the division return zero no matter what and so one can arbitrarily inflate the b_x and b_y term which are supposedly degree bounds.

Vikram said he'll send me the counter-example proof soon, but I think the fix is clear

@Katy Hristova @František Silváši 🦉 @Julian Sutherland
Ah interesting! I hadn't finished reviewing everything that the request returned so I should go and finish that to see if anything else came up.
@Quang Dao Thanks for bringing this to our attention, myself and @Katy Hristova submitted a very small PR here to fix this. Please review :pray:
